en.title: Immunity
en.who: Guests who mark catching every cold going around, kids bringing everything home, getting sick after a busy stretch, getting sick after short sleep, a trip or flu season coming up, or only taking vitamin C once a cold starts.
studyWhy: why health management is about immunity
most illness starts in the gut

say: I totally get it. Someone at work sneezes, and a few days later it's you. Or you push through a crazy busy stretch, and the moment it's over, you're the one in bed.
feel.tip: Say back what they marked, in their words. Then ask: "When does it usually get you?"

say: Honestly, I've been there. [Your story in a line or two: when it was, what it felt like, what you tried that didn't work.]
felt.tip: Your own story, or someone close to you ("my mom", "a friend from work"). No story yet? "A lot of the people I talk to say exactly the same thing." Never make one up.

say: What I learned is that the immune system isn't a muscle you can pump up. It rebuilds itself every day, a big part of it lives in the gut, and the vitamins only help as a daily habit, not once the cold has already started.
So this is what I'd start with.
found.tip: One or two sentences from Part A, then the routine. Pick the products that match what they marked.

en.ask: Based on what you told me, I'd start with the Probiotic, the daily Vitamin C, and a scoop of protein at breakfast. Do you want to take it home tonight?
en.doctor: A fever for more than three days, trouble breathing, infections that keep coming back, or any fever in a baby under three months? See a doctor first.
know: Immunity isn't something you boost. It's something you don't let run short.
The immune system rebuilds itself every day, and it struggles when it runs short or gets overloaded. Nothing stops every cold, so be wary of anyone who says it does.
A big part of the immune system lives in the gut.

When the gut is out of balance, the immune system is busy with trouble at home and has less left for the cold going around. In a review of 24 trials, people on probiotics caught about a quarter fewer colds (low certainty).
Sleep has the hardest numbers of anything here.
In one study everyone was exposed to the same cold virus. People sleeping under six hours were about four times more likely to catch it than people sleeping over seven.
Antibodies and white blood cells are made of protein.

The front-line cells are replaced within days, so the supply has to arrive every day. In a busy week breakfast is toast or nothing, and the supply runs short right when you need it most. One scoop adds 21 g.
Vitamin C is a daily habit, not a rescue.

Across 29 trials, vitamin C taken every day made colds about 8 percent shorter in adults and 14 percent in children. Started once the cold began, it showed no consistent benefit. Vitamin D is the same: steady doses, and the most benefit for people who were low.
Some products are for a stretch, not all year.
The zinc tablet is for deadline weeks when sleep slips, echinacea for a trip or the peak of flu season. Too much zinc for months pulls copper down, so keep zinc from all sources under 40 mg a day.
Fried food, smoke and alcohol keep a low hum of inflammation going all day.

Inflammation is how the immune system protects you, but that background hum competes with the real job. Colourful fruit and vegetables help keep it down; capsules are a floor for busy weeks, not a replacement for eating your greens.
The free half of the plan.

Twenty seconds of handwashing when you get home and before you eat cut colds by 16 to 21 percent in community programs. Add seven hours of sleep and a steady bedtime, most of all in the week before a trip or a vaccine.
routine: A scoop of Plant Protein, Double X, Vitamin C Extended Release and Vitamin D
Once a day, with cool water
Probiotic, plus Prebiotic Fiber stirred into water or coffee
Twenty seconds with g&h Protect Hand Soap
The evening Double X, and Magnesium
Seven hours, the same bedtime every night
Immunity Echinacea, Twist Tubes, Hand Sanitizer in the bag; then stop

zh.title: 免疫力
zh.who: 适合在问卷里勾了别人一感冒就中招、孩子一上学全家轮着病、一忙完就病倒、一熬夜就感冒、要出门旅行或流感季快到了，或者感冒了才想起吃维C的客人。

say: 我特别懂。办公室有人打个喷嚏，过几天就轮到你了。或者拼命忙完一阵，刚一放松，人就倒下了。
feel.tip: 用对方自己的话，把问卷上勾的说回去。然后问一句：“一般是什么时候最容易中招？”

say: 说实话，我也经历过。[你的故事，一两句就好：什么时候、什么感觉、试过什么没用。]
felt.tip: 讲你自己的，或者身边人的（“我妈妈”“我一个同事”）。还没有故事？就说：“我身边很多朋友也是这样。”千万别编。

say: 我后来学到，免疫力不是肌肉，练不大。它每天都在自我更新，很大一部分就在肠道里，而营养素要每天吃才有用，等感冒来了才吃，帮不了多少。
所以，我会先从这个开始。
found.tip: 从 Part A 挑一两句讲，然后讲作息。挑跟对方勾的对得上的产品。

zh.ask: 按你刚才说的，我建议先从益生菌、每天的维C，还有早餐加一勺蛋白粉开始。今天要不要先带回去？
zh.doctor: 发烧超过三天、呼吸困难、感染反反复复，或者三个月以下的宝宝发烧，请先去看医生。
know: 免疫力不是用来“提升”的，是不能让它缺。
免疫系统每天都在自我更新，原料一短缺、负担一重，它就力不从心。没有什么能让人一次感冒都不得，谁这么说都要小心。
免疫系统很大一部分在肠道里。
肠道一乱，免疫系统光处理家里的事就忙不过来，外面传来的感冒自然顾不上。一篇汇总24个试验的综述里，吃益生菌的人感冒少了大约四分之一（证据确定性较低）。
在所有办法里，睡眠的数据最硬。
有研究让一群人接触同一种感冒病毒，每晚睡不到六小时的人，中招的几率大约是睡满七小时的四倍。
抗体和白细胞都是蛋白质做的。
冲在最前面的免疫细胞几天就换一批，所以原料得每天送到。一忙起来，早餐不是一片面包就是干脆不吃，偏偏在最需要的时候断了供。一勺蛋白粉就有21克。
维C是日常习惯，不是救急用的。
汇总29个试验的结果，每天吃维C，成人感冒缩短约8%，孩子约14%；感冒了才开始吃，看不出稳定的效果。维生素D也一样：稳定地吃，本来就缺的人受益最大。
有些东西是阶段性用的，不是一年到头吃。
锌片留给赶项目、睡不够的那几周，紫锥菊留给出行和流感高峰。锌吃太多、吃太久会把铜拉低，所有来源加起来，每天不超过40毫克。
油炸、烟、酒，会让身体整天开着低度炎症。
炎症本来是免疫系统保护你的方式，但这层背景噪音会跟真正的任务抢资源。五颜六色的蔬果能把它压下来，胶囊是忙的那几周的保底，不是用来代替吃菜的。
方案里免费的那一半。
到家、吃饭前洗满二十秒手，社区洗手项目让感冒少了16%到21%。再守住七小时睡眠和固定的上床时间，出门或打疫苗前的那一周尤其要守住。
routine: 一勺有机植物蛋白粉，加双X、维生素C缓释片和维生素D
益生菌，加益生元纤维粉，冲进水或咖啡里
睡满七小时，每天同一时间上床
紫锥菊免疫片、随身营养饮管，包里放一瓶免洗洗手液；过了就停
